subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should cron quarantine recovery preserve earlier invalid records through a bounded retained archive/migration path, or should an over-cap sidecar fail closed and require explicit Doctor recovery instead of overwriting prior recovery data?
rationale: Both options bound memory and disk growth, but they differ in whether malformed persisted jobs remain recoverable after repeated overflows; that is a user-data and recovery-policy choice rather than a mechanical fix.

options.title: Use bounded retained recovery
options.body: Preserve prior quarantined records with an explicit bounded retention or migration design, then start a new active sidecar without silently discarding earlier entries.

options.title: Fail closed for recovery
options.body: Reject the over-cap save without rotating files and direct users to an explicit Doctor repair flow, preserving the existing recovery record intact.

recommendation.title: Use bounded retained recovery
recommendation.body: Preserve prior quarantined records with an explicit bounded retention or migration design, then start a new active sidecar without silently discarding earlier entries.
